purpose: Separate automatic/read-only ConfigData Lookup validation from explicit Stage 6 materialization writer authority without changing Stage 0-6 materialization semantics or package CLI authority.

writerProofPolicy.reason: CLR5 proves authority separation. A synthetic ConfigData/index mutation solely to force a writer commit would violate the frozen semantic/materialization boundary. Writer behavior reuses the already validated Stage 6 rebuild algorithm and is guarded structurally; a future legitimate stale materialization may exercise the explicit writer without reopening CLR5.

reviews.detail: npm run lookup/refs/find remains on the legacy Stage 5 CLI until CLR7 cutover.
Legacy Stage 7/8 orchestration remains unchanged and outside the NEW ConfigData Lookup owner authority.
The explicit writer is not forced to create a synthetic materialization change while Stage 6 is clean. A future legitimate stale input can exercise it without changing CLR5 completion.

nextStart: After CLR5 freeze, begin CLR6 shadow/parity verification between the preserved Stage 0-6 behavior and the NEW ConfigData Lookup surface. Do not cut over package CLI or retire Stage 7/8 authority until CLR7.
reopenConditions: An automatic or required validation path regains contents:write, rebuild execution, commit, or push authority.
The explicit writer can target main or gh-pages, or can run without workflow_dispatch confirmation and --apply.
The writer reimplements Stage 0-6 materialization semantics instead of delegating to the frozen Stage 6 rebuild algorithm.
Project Check cannot route ConfigData Lookup validation/writer tooling to the dedicated configdata-lookup owner.
